Copy-mode command dispatch snapshots the Copy mouse_event after its initial cursor update. Begin-selection and scroll-to-mouse read only that snapshot; drag callbacks use their own later event parameters. None retains the previous absent-mouse meaning.
A caller-scoped borrow of an existing Rc handle. The field neither owns nor releases an additional model reference; the lifetime bounds its access to the caller operation.
Synchronous copy-mode dispatch borrows a locally retained session. The outer callback releases that owner through session_remove_ref after all inner early-return paths, preserving deferred cleanup.
Synchronous command context observes the session-owned RefBox link; absence is allocation-free and expiration cannot resolve to a reused link address. Legacy pointer uses remain operation-bounded.
All copy-mode command descriptor names are C literals, consumed synchronously by table lookup.

The mode observes the floating pane's Box-owned editor through a weak pane and unique editor ID. Spawn returns the handle after installing the editor. PID and cancellation resolve only a matching live slot; completion compares the detached editor's ID before clearing mode state. A stale handle cannot cancel a replacement. Evidence: src/shared/spawn.rs EditorHandle; src/spawn.rs spawn_editor and stale_editor_handle_does_not_cancel_replacement.

Options roots, entries and array items are Box-owned; these links observe parent or selected option storage during replacement and callbacks. Weak<T> cannot target those Boxes. A model-handle plus option-name/key resolver may work for some callers, but globals, nested options and removal need a separate consistent identity design. Evidence: src/options.rs options_create_owned, options_add, options_remove, options_array_clear; src/hooks.rs; src/window_customize.rs.
